previous_blocking_reason: Recorded as 'no docker daemon in this environment'. That reason was inaccurate: the docker, dockerd, containerd and runc binaries were all present; the daemon had simply not been started. The FAIL verdict itself was correct - LG3 had genuinely not been demonstrated - but the reason attached to it was wrong. See reports/LAB_001_LG3_BUILD_EVIDENCE.md.

image.not_reproducible_artifact: the exported OCI tarball bytes differ between builds (archive wrapper metadata), while every blob inside is identical. Verify the manifest digest, never the tarball.

superseded_digests.sha256:6edd71a6adff7eab4fca99b9b8fb2e929: 11 layers. The Dockerfile before calibration/ and pricing/ were added. build.sh at HEAD can no longer produce it. Recorded because the first LG3 evidence quotes it.
superseded_digests.sha256:780e1f2518e6abb66bb0f824f853a501a: 13 layers, but a pre-E027 blind.py, no judge.py, and a calibration fixture matching no commit. The first dry run stamped this digest on its records, and the Reproduction Agent proved that image cannot produce them - re-running inside it gives 9 completed, not 10. This is why container_digest is now recorded alongside a self-derived image_content_sha256.

runtime.dependency_manifest_recipe: harness/attest.py:dependency_manifest_hash - sha256 over sorted 'name==version\n' lines for every installed distribution, names lowercased with underscores normalised to hyphens. The previous value (93d9ecce...) was computed by no code and documented by no recipe; the Reproduction Agent tried six plausible derivations and matched none.
runtime.image_content_recipe: harness/attest.py:image_content_hash - computed INSIDE the running container over harness/, run_record_schema.json, requirements.lock.txt, calibration/ and pricing/. Unlike container_digest it cannot be forged by a command-line flag.

build.dockerignore: present, and its patterns are **/-prefixed. Docker ignore patterns match against paths relative to the context root, so a bare `__pycache__/` matches only a top-level one and silently misses harness/__pycache__/. Measured: without the prefix a contaminated tree still produced a different digest. See EVIDENCE_LEDGER E029.

clean_rebuild.procedure: docker system prune -a -f && docker buildx prune -a -f, base image re-pulled by digest from an empty store, rebuilt with --no-cache
clean_rebuild.first_attempt_root_cause: pip compiled bytecode at install time; each .pyc embeds the source file's mtime (the build wall clock) in its 16-byte header, so bodies were identical and headers differed by one byte at offset 8. BuildKit rewrite-timestamp rewrites tar header mtimes and cannot reach a timestamp inside a file's own bytes.
clean_rebuild.fix: pip install --no-compile, plus an explicit __pycache__ sweep
clean_rebuild.verified_on: final image, after a full prune and base re-pull from an empty store

hardening_applied: the apt-get layer was removed entirely: it installed git, curl, jq and ca-certificates with loose version globs, and the base image already ships ca-certificates while shipping none of the network tools
no general-purpose network client (git, curl, wget, jq, nc, ssh) exists inside the measured container
the build is hermetic: --network=none, all wheels installed from a vendored wheelhouse with --no-index
candidates_installed_note: NONE. No candidate is installed in this image. Candidates are added per-run from their pinned commit SHA under CANDIDATE_RUNTIME_PROFILES.md, and four of the seven non-failed candidates are currently blocked on an incomplete runtime profile.
what_this_does_not_establish: no benchmark run has been performed
